title: German Cities — Opportunity-Card (Chancenkarte) Relocation Scoreboard
subtitle: Scored for an experienced Bangladeshi software engineer (4y+ .NET/Python, distributed systems, AI/RAG, enterprise integration): job-search visa → full-time job + EU Blue Card → permanent residency → naturalisation

columns.label: Mid-level job market & sponsors
columns.description: Depth of full-time demand and visa-sponsoring employers for an experienced (4y+) .NET / Python / AI-RAG / enterprise-integration engineer — enterprise and corporate employers weigh heavily; junior-generalist volume weighs less. Federal data show 59% of 2024 IT vacancies target the 'Experte' level, so experienced hiring is the favourable slice.

columns.label: Chancenkarte → Blue Card conversion
columns.description: Evidence-backed local risk from complete application to permission for full-time Blue Card employment. Appointment waits, authority decision time and eAT production are kept separate; missing official timing is scored conservatively.

columns.label: City registration (Anmeldung)
columns.description: Ease of registering the main residence, which establishes the responsible foreigners authority and supplies residence evidence commonly requested for the Blue Card application.

columns.label: Part-time / any-field odd jobs
columns.description: Depth of the any-field ≤20 h/week gig market the Chancenkarte permits — gastro, warehouse/logistics, delivery, retail — accessible without German fluency. Bigger population plus a logistics/hospitality base scores higher; 2026 minimum wage €13.90/h.

columns.label: Housing + rent affordability
columns.description: New-lease rent level and how findable a flat is for a newcomer with no SCHUFA (higher score = cheaper and easier).

columns.label: English usability (work + admin)
columns.description: How far English carries you across the full-time job market and bureaucracy (part-time odd jobs no longer depend on it). English-OK developer roles are heavily concentrated in Berlin and Munich.

columns.label: Safety & xenophobia climate
columns.description: Physical safety plus far-right / anti-Muslim risk for a visible-minority Muslim couple; anti-Muslim hate crime in Germany is predominantly far-right in origin, so regional far-right strength is the main differentiator.

columns.label: Competition / your odds (mid-level)
columns.description: Applicant saturation for the roles you can realistically land (higher = better odds). Federal data show the 2024 saturation is concentrated among under-35 juniors, so an experienced candidate faces easier odds than a fresh graduate — tempered where English-OK roles are scarce.

columns.label: Cost of living
columns.description: Non-rent burn rate — higher score = cheaper, longer runway on part-time income while job-searching.

columns.label: Connectivity & facilities
columns.description: Air links to Dhaka (all 1-stop at best) plus public transport.

detail.summary: The best all-rounder for this plan — no weak link in the land-and-convert core, and a strong any-field part-time base.
detail.note: Official decision time circa 4–8 weeks (authority processing after a complete application); the appointment intake wait and Bundesdruckerei eAT production are extra and unpublished. The Hamburg Welcome Center for Professionals runs a dedicated skilled-worker channel. The conversion score reflects documented local process risk and evidence quality; naturalisation is not scored.

pros.text: The Hamburg Welcome Center for Professionals runs a dedicated, English-friendly skilled-worker channel; the authority publishes a circa 4–8 week decision time (processing after a complete application — not counting the appointment wait or eAT card production).
Sponsor-heavy market (Airbus, Otto/About You, Google, gaming, growing AI/climatetech) that fits an enterprise-integration + AI profile; rents well below Munich/Frankfurt.
Port-and-logistics plus hospitality give a deep any-field part-time market; diverse, western, low far-right risk with a real Bangladeshi anchor.

cons.text: Deep-tech/AI-research depth trails Berlin/Munich; English-OK developer roles are a thin slice (~6 on EnglishJobs.de).
Naturalisation backlog (~26,000 pending, ~14 months) makes the citizenship tail slow; Anmeldung slots go fast.

methodology: Overall is the weighted mean of 11 scored criteria, computed live with raw 0–100 scores. The immediate land-and-convert decision dominates: Jobs (18) + Chancenkarte-to-Blue-Card conversion (22) + Anmeldung (12) = 52 points. Conversion scores separate application intake, authority decision or employment authorisation, and physical eAT production; a published printing time is never treated as the total wait. Official end-to-end authority timings receive the highest confidence. Official vague warnings or partial-stage timings receive medium confidence. Where the responsible authority publishes no total time, the UI says so and the score is conservative rather than inventing precision. An authority that transparently publishes a slow official time is scored on that documented duration and its channel design, not penalised below authorities that publish nothing — non-publication paired with disclosed pressure is scored conservatively, never rewarded for opacity. A timely application before expiry preserves lawful residence under §81(4) AufenthG, but the Opportunity Card's existing 20-hour work restriction normally continues until the authority authorises the future full-time employment; under §81(5a), future-title employment is permitted once issuance has been initiated and must be recorded in the interim certificate. Naturalisation and settlement queues are descriptive context only and do not affect city scores. Federal 2026 constants: Blue Card salary €50,700 standard / €45,934.20 for shortage and IT occupations; Opportunity Card funds €1,091 per month and work up to 20 hours weekly during search.
caveats: A four-month conversion wait is plausible and Munich now officially warns that EU Blue Card processing can take up to seven months. Do not sign an unconditional immediate full-time start date without confirming work authorisation.
Most cities do not publish an end-to-end Opportunity Card-to-Blue Card service level. Low-confidence scores compare process design and disclosed pressure, not guaranteed personal waiting times.
The eAT card's 4–6 week production period begins after a positive decision or appointment and is not the same as the application queue.

Apply with a complete pack immediately after the offer: job offer or contract, Erklärung zum Beschäftigungsverhältnis, passport and current title, recognised degree/anabin or ZAB evidence, Anmeldung/residence evidence, health insurance, and salary/job-description evidence.
Naturalisation is intentionally unscored. Its office may be organisationally separate and its backlog does not reliably predict employment-residence processing.
